strengths.value: First method to quantize 100B+ parameter LLMs (OPT-175B, BLOOM-176B) to 3-4 bits in roughly four GPU hours with negligible perplexity loss.

ev.quote: GPTQ can quantize GPT models with 175 billion parameters in approximately four GPU hours, reducing the bitwidth down to 3 or 4 bits per weight, with negligible accuracy degradation

strengths.value: Real end-to-end decoding speedups: 3.25x on A100 and 4.5x on A6000 over FP16 via custom mixed-precision GPU kernels.

ev.quote: end-to-end inference speedups over FP16, of around 3.25x when using high-end GPUs (NVIDIA A100) and 4.5x when using more cost-effective ones (NVIDIA A6000)

strengths.value: Pushes one-shot extreme quantization to 2-bit and ternary regimes, with under 1.5 PPL drop on OPT-175B at 2.2-bit grouping.

ev.quote: At ≈ 2.2 bit (group-size 128; using FP16 scale and 2-bit zero point per group) the perplexity increase is already less than 1.5 points

strengths.value: Open-source code released, with reproducibility statement listing CUDA kernels and full evaluation pipeline.

ev.quote: The implementation is available at https://github.com/IST-DASLab/gptq

weaknesses.value: No speedup on the actual matrix multiplications because mainstream hardware lacks mixed FP16xINT4 multiply support.

ev.quote: our method currently does not provide speedups for the actual multiplications, due to the lack of hardware support for mixed-precision operands (e.g. FP16 x INT4) on mainstream architectures

weaknesses.value: Activations are not quantized, so memory and compute savings are limited to the weight stream.

ev.quote: our current results do not include activation quantization, as they are not a significant bottleneck in our target scenarios

weaknesses.value: Speedups come only from reduced memory movement, not from any reduction in arithmetic operations.

ev.quote: our method obtains speedups from reduced memory movement, and does not lead to computational reductions

weaknesses.value: Quality is judged by perplexity only; bias and other secondary effects of compression are not studied.

ev.quote: our study focused on "leading accuracy" metrics that are standard in the literature, such as perplexity ... a thorough study of the impact of compression upon secondary measures, and in particular bias effects ... is warranted

limitations.value: Tested only on data-centre GPUs (A100, A6000); no edge or mobile deployment is evaluated.
Kernels target only batch-size-1 generative inference; large-batch and prefill scenarios are not optimised.

ev.quote: our kernels target generative inference in the low batch-size setting (for simplicity, we consider only batchsize 1)

limitations.value: Safety, jailbreak, and toxicity behaviour after compression are not measured; evaluation focuses on language modelling.

ev.quote: our study focused on "leading accuracy" metrics that are standard in the literature, such as perplexity

limitations.value: Long-context behaviour is not evaluated; perplexity uses fixed 2048-token windows.

ev.quote: the sequence is split into non-overlapping segments of width 2048, the full context size of our models

future_work_stated.value: Add activation quantization on top of GPTQ using orthogonal techniques such as ZeroQuant.

ev.quote: our study focuses on generative tasks, and does not consider activation quantization. These are natural directions for future work

future_work_stated.value: Build carefully designed GPU kernels to convert memory savings into computational reductions.

ev.quote: we believe this can be achieved with carefully-designed GPU kernels and existing techniques

future_work_stated.value: Study the effect of compression on bias and other secondary safety measures.

ev.quote: a thorough study of the impact of compression upon secondary measures, and in particular bias effects (Bender et al., 2021) is warranted
